scenes.heading: Query Optimization
scenes.narration: Query optimization is the art of restructuring queries and data so the engine reads less, shuffles less, and computes less to return the same result faster.

scenes.heading: High-impact techniques
bullets: Prune partitions and push filters down early
Select only the columns you need
Prefer broadcast joins for small tables
scenes.narration: The biggest wins come from reading less data: prune partitions with filters on partition columns and push predicates down so the scan drops rows early. Selecting only required columns lets columnar formats skip unread data entirely. For joins, broadcasting a small table to every node avoids an expensive shuffle. And pre-aggregating or caching frequently requested results turns repeated heavy queries into cheap lookups.

scenes.heading: Reading the plan and fixing a query
scenes.code:
-- Inspect the physical plan first
EXPLAIN
SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.amount) AS total
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'   -- prunes partitions
  AND c.region = 'EU'                      -- filter pushed down
GROUP BY o.customer_id;
-- small customers table -> hint a broadcast join
-- SELECT /*+ BROADCAST(c) */ ...
scenes.narration: Always start by reading the query plan with EXPLAIN so you can see how the engine intends to execute it. Here the date predicate on the partitioned order_date column lets the engine prune whole partitions instead of scanning all history. The region filter is pushed down so rows are dropped as early as possible. Because the customers table is small, hinting a broadcast join sends it to every node and avoids shuffling the large orders table. Together these choices dramatically cut the data read and moved.

scenes.heading: How the optimizer works
steps: Parse SQL to a logical plan
Choose join order and physical ops
scenes.narration: The optimizer first parses your SQL into a logical plan describing what to compute. It applies rewrite rules such as predicate pushdown and constant folding to simplify that plan. Using table statistics like row counts and cardinality, it estimates the cost of alternative strategies. It then chooses a join order and concrete physical operators, for example a broadcast versus a shuffle join. Finally the engine executes the plan it judged cheapest, which is only as good as the statistics behind it.

scenes.heading: Common anti-patterns to fix
bullets: SELECT star drags in unused columns
Functions on filter columns block pruning
scenes.narration: Many slow queries share the same avoidable mistakes. Selecting every column with SELECT star pulls in data you never use and defeats columnar skipping. Wrapping a partition or filter column in a function prevents the engine from pruning, so it scans everything. Joins on the wrong or missing keys can explode into a near cartesian product. And stale statistics lead the optimizer to pick poor join orders and strategies, so refreshing statistics after big loads is one of the cheapest wins available.

scenes.text: Read the plan, keep statistics fresh, and the winning move is almost always reading and shuffling less data.
scenes.narration: Make a habit of reading the execution plan and keeping table statistics fresh, because the winning optimization is almost always structuring the query and data so the engine reads and shuffles less.
